risks.title: No certified real-environment adapters
risks.description: The Oracle SQL, diagnostic-file and OS adapters are DISABLED or CONTRACT_ONLY; only synthetic fixtures run. Someone could mistake the framework release for production readiness.
risks.mitigation: The registry, the release gate and the docs keep READY_FOR_REAL_ENVIRONMENT_PILOT at NO until a pilot record exists.
risks.closure_condition: An approved subproject implements a real adapter, it passes an integration pilot in an approved non-production environment and the administrator accepts it.

risks.title: Local stdio does not authenticate the person
risks.description: The MCP transport is a local stdio pipe: protection is the operating-system account and file permissions of the host, not an identity check on the caller.
risks.mitigation: Run the gateway under a dedicated least-privilege account, restrict repository and evidence directory permissions, keep it off shared hosts.
risks.closure_condition: The security reviewer attests the host access controls for the pilot host, or an authenticated transport is designed and approved.

risks.title: Approvals are structural declarations
risks.description: Approval records are checked for structure, digest and separation of proposer and reviewer, but this repository has no authentication or signature mechanism.
risks.mitigation: Approvals happen in Git review by named humans; releases are tagged only by a human after review.
risks.closure_condition: A mechanism that verifies approver identity outside the repository (for example signed commits or an external change system) is adopted.

risks.title: Sanitization is heuristic
risks.description: Secret detection and signature handling in the sanitizer are heuristics biased to over-redact; unknown formats could still slip through or hide useful data.
risks.mitigation: Default-deny per-field policy, free text is DROP-only, unknown signatures are tokenized, mutation tests guard the defenses.
risks.closure_condition: A review of sanitizer behavior on anonymized real samples is completed during an approved pilot.

risks.title: Local MCP is not a local model
risks.description: Sanitized evidence returned to the MCP client may be processed outside the workstation depending on the client product configuration.
risks.mitigation: Evidence is minimized before it leaves the gateway and nothing raw is ever returned.
risks.closure_condition: A data-flow assessment of the chosen client and its retention terms is approved.

risks.title: Evidence packages prove integrity, not authenticity
risks.description: Hashes and fingerprints detect alteration but do not identify who produced a package; someone able to regenerate all files consistently is not stopped.
risks.mitigation: Independent human review of the log and manifest; packages are kept outside the repository with the raw log retained separately.
risks.closure_condition: Evidence is produced by a controlled pipeline with provenance or is signed.

risks.title: Only Windows with Git Bash has been validated
risks.description: The full regression and the gate were executed on Windows with Git Bash and Python 3.13; Linux and macOS were not tested.
risks.mitigation: The limitation is stated in the readiness documents; the gate must be run on each target platform before a pilot there.
risks.closure_condition: The release gate passes on each platform the administrator intends to use.

risks.title: Certified SQL was never executed against a real database
risks.description: Queries are statically certified (read-only guard, contract fields) and exercised only through fixtures; real execution may reveal dictionary or version differences.
risks.mitigation: Per-collector version and license gates, R0 read-only rule, capability degradation when facts are unknown.
risks.closure_condition: Each collector is executed read-only in an approved non-production environment and the result is recorded in a pilot record.

risks.title: Fixtures may drift from real outputs
risks.description: Synthetic fixtures encode the shapes the parsers and collectors expect; real outputs can differ in ways the tests cannot reveal.
risks.mitigation: Schema validation at the adapter boundary treats every adapter output as untrusted and fails closed on unexpected shapes.
risks.closure_condition: Fixtures are compared with anonymized real outputs during a pilot.
